messages:
Maggie Chen: quick check-in re: client-hinted precision negotiation. thinking we should standardize a small hint header (latency|quality|balanced) and have runtime map that to precision lanes (fp8/int8/4bit) + fallback policy. thoughts?
José Alvarez: +1 for hint header. question: how do we prevent callers from gaming quality by lying they want 'quality' for cheaper routes?
Sam Patel: two quick levers: (1) account-tier enforcement (only enterprise can request quality lane by default), (2) runtime budget checks — we can rate-limit high-quality assignments per API key.
Kaira Nair: agree with Sam. also we need to consider caching/KV cache cold-starts. mixing precisions for same model shards will invalidate prefixes, hurting latency not helping it.
Maggie Chen: good call on cache. propose: precision assignment is per-request but key is appended to cache key: e.g., cache_key := base_key + ":p=" + precision_lane. so different lanes have disjoint caches. we accept cost hit initially.
José Alvarez: that solves correctness. but we should expose the assigned lane in response headers for observability. e.g., x-rw-assigned-precision: int8
Sam Patel: example hint header proposal: `x-rw-precision-hint: latency|quality|balanced`. runtime mapping table (config): {"latency":"4bit","balanced":"int8","quality":"fp8"}. can be overridden per-model.
Kaira Nair: runtime implications: batching scheduler must group by precision lane to avoid mixing kernels and forcing config switches. so add a per-lane queue in the scheduler.
Ben Ops: ops note: per-lane queues affect capacity accounting. we need to add per-lane GPU utilization metrics + billing tags. otherwise cost attribution is impossible.
quant-bot: telemetry suggestion: emit `precision_assigned` (fp8/int8/4bit), `precision_hint`, `model_version`, `cache_hit` as tags on request spans.
Maggie Chen: rollout plan idea: feature-flagged, opt-in per-customer. Phase 1: response header + telemetry only. Phase 2: soft-assignment for canary customers (5% traffic), Phase 3: broader rollout with tier controls.
José Alvarez: safety nets: auto-fallback on quality regressions. define a degradation score threshold that triggers fallback to safer precision. do we already have degscore?
Sam Patel: we do; wire it to the per-endpoint rollout. if degscore delta > 0.05 within a window, automatically move those customers to higher-fidelity lane.
Kaira Nair: tests: need A/B prompt set for each model to validate quality across lanes. add a synthetic eval harness that runs on canary traffic.
Ben Ops: deployment ops: ensure each precision variant has a warmup path for KV caches. plan: pre-warm on canary nodes 1h before traffic cutover. also add an emergency toggle to force full-precision fallback.
Maggie Chen: policy for untrusted requests: unknown API keys or public endpoints default to 'balanced' lane. explicit 'quality' requires account flag.
José Alvarez: minor interface detail: should the client hint be optional in SDKs? make it opt-in. default behavior unchanged.
Sam Patel: sample SDK header snippet for fetch: `headers: {"x-rw-precision-hint":"latency"}`. runtime returns `x-rw-assigned-precision: 4bit` and `x-rw-precision-reason: "tier-default"`
Kaira Nair: ops metric additions: tokens_by_precision, p95_latency_by_precision, degscore_by_precision. need dashboards & alerts for degscore spikes per lane.
Maggie Chen: action items: Jose to spec header + enforcement rules, Sam to update scheduler + batching lanes, Kaira to create eval harness and dashboards, Ben to draft ops runbook + toggles. I'll own the rollout doc.
José Alvarez: I'll start a tiny RFC with config examples and enforcement table.
Sam Patel: I'll mount per-lane queues in scheduler branch tonight, pinging @kaira for integration tests.
Kaira Nair: will prepare eval prompts and a small telem dashboard.
Ben Ops: will add emergency fallback toggle in the console and update runbook.
Maggie Chen: great. small note: keep default token pricing unchanged until we observe real cost delta. we can add per-precision pricing later once telemetry is solid. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
José Alvarez: one more: document how canary telemetry maps to billing so finance can review when we propose pricing changes.
Maggie Chen: noted. thanks all :wave:
